report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/kairos/drafts.py chunk 1 of 1: draft persistence with path-traversal guards, lifecycle statuses, and apply_payload handoff.

handoff.purpose: Persist advisory drafts as JSON files and provide lifecycle operations (list, get, delete, set_status, apply_payload).

symbols.name: ROOT
symbols.note: Repository root path, parents[2] of this file.

symbols.name: DRAFT_DIR
symbols.note: Directory for draft files under runs/drafts.

symbols.name: _SLUG_RE
symbols.note: Regex to replace non-alphanumeric chars with hyphen.

symbols.name: _ID_RE
symbols.note: Regex for valid draft id stems: alphanumeric, dot, underscore, hyphen, 1-120 chars.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Sanitize text into a slug, max_len 48, fallback 'draft'.

symbols.name: _safe_path
symbols.note: Resolve draft id to path only if it matches _ID_RE and stays inside DRAFT_DIR.

symbols.name: save_draft
symbols.note: Write a draft JSON file with unique timestamp-slug name.

symbols.name: list_drafts
symbols.note: Return newest-first summaries of all draft files.

symbols.name: get_draft
symbols.note: Read and return a draft dict by id, or None.

symbols.name: delete_draft
symbols.note: Delete a draft file by id, returns True if deleted.

symbols.name: _STATUSES
symbols.note: Tuple of valid statuses: pending, applied, dismissed.

symbols.name: set_status
symbols.note: Transition a draft's status, raising on invalid status, idempotent.

symbols.name: apply_payload
symbols.note: Return a review packet for a draft and mark it applied.

claims.text: Persist advisory drafts -- the missing half of the FrugalGPT loop (Era 3 #1).
claims.why: This claim references an external concept (FrugalGPT loop, Era 3) not present in this chunk.

claims.text: An advisory-mode task legitimately writes nothing: the free lane produces a PROPOSAL that a write-capable, trusted lane (Claude / the user) applies later.
claims.why: The distinction between advisory-mode and write-capable lanes is not defined in this chunk; the code only persists drafts.

claims.text: Until now that proposal lived only inside the offload result and evaporated when the caller dropped it.
claims.why: References previous behavior not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Here every accepted advisory report is persisted to ``runs/drafts/<ts>-<slug>.json`` so it can be listed, reviewed, applied, and cleaned up later -- ``daedalus drafts list|show|rm``.
claims.why: save_draft writes to DRAFT_DIR (runs/drafts) with timestamp-slug filename; list_drafts, get_draft, delete_draft support listing, showing, and removing.

claims.text: Apply is deliberately NOT automated: a draft is a proposal, and the safety model says a free model may propose but never merge. Applying stays a human / Claude action (Era-3 follow-up wires it into the webapp queue view).
claims.why: apply_payload does not write to the target repo; it only marks status 'applied' and returns a packet with a handoff message instructing human/Claude to apply.

claims.text: This module moved one package level deeper. Runtime state remains at the repository root for backward compatibility with every existing draft.
claims.why: The previous location is not visible in this chunk; only the current ROOT computation is shown.

claims.text: A draft id is our own timestamp-slug stem. It arrives from the CLI and from URL path segments (/api/drafts/<id>/apply), so it MUST NOT be trusted into a filesystem path -- reject anything that isn't a plain stem (no separators, no traversal). Closes the path-traversal gap Minos would have flagged.
claims.why: _ID_RE allows only [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,120} which excludes slashes, backslashes, and traversal sequences; _safe_path further resolves and checks containment under DRAFT_DIR.

claims.text: Resolve a draft id to its file ONLY if the id is a plain stem that stays inside DRAFT_DIR. Returns None for anything suspicious (``..``, separators, absolute paths, symlink escapes).
claims.why: The regex rejects '..' and separators; resolve().relative_to(DRAFT_DIR.resolve()) catches symlink escapes and absolute paths via ValueError/OSError.

claims.text: Write one accepted advisory report to the drafts store; returns the path.
claims.why: save_draft creates DRAFT_DIR, constructs a unique path, writes JSON, and returns the path.

claims.text: never overwrite an existing draft from the same second
claims.why: The while loop checks path.exists() and appends a counter suffix until a non-existing path is found.

claims.text: Newest-first summaries of every stored draft.
claims.why: Files are sorted with reverse=True on the glob results, which sorts lexicographically; since timestamps are in YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ format, lexicographic order corresponds to chronological order, so reverse gives newest-first.

claims.text: Transition a draft's lifecycle. Returns the updated draft, or None if the id is unknown; raises ValueError on an invalid status. This does NOT touch the filesystem of the target repo -- 'applied' only marks the proposal as handled (a free model may propose, never merge; the actual edit is a human / Claude action). Idempotent.
claims.why: set_status raises ValueError for invalid status, returns None for unknown id, only writes to the draft file (not the target repo), and setting the same status again simply rewrites the same value (idempotent).

claims.text: The review packet a human / the Claude lane needs to ACTUALLY apply a draft: the objective, the target paths, and the proposal text. Marks the draft 'applied' (handled) but performs no write itself -- returning the packet IS the handoff. None if the id is unknown.
claims.why: apply_payload calls get_draft, returns None if unknown, builds a packet with objective, paths, proposal, etc., calls set_status to mark applied, and performs no write to the target repo.

claims.text: A check that CANNOT FAIL: an assertion comparing something with itself, a test whose fixture is derived from the thing under test, a branch no input reaches.
claims.where: no such check in this chunk
claims.why: No self-comparison assertions or self-derived fixtures exist in this chunk.

claims.text: A refusal with NO REACHABLE REPAIR: code that reports an error and names a fix another rule in this same file forbids.
claims.where: no such refusal in this chunk
claims.why: No error messages or refusal patterns exist in this chunk.

claims.text: A rule INVERTED with respect to its own stated goal: it blocks the narrow precise action and permits the broad one.
claims.where: no such rule in this chunk
claims.why: The path validation blocks broad actions (traversal) and permits narrow ones (plain stems), which is consistent with its goal.

claims.text: A value parsed from output whose FORMAT IS NOT PINNED: a parser that will silently report 'absent' rather than 'unreadable' when its input changes shape.
claims.where: no such parser in this chunk
claims.why: The JSON parsing in list_drafts/get_draft/set_status catches JSONDecodeError and returns None or skips, which could be seen as 'unreadable' but does not report 'absent' explicitly; however, the format of the JSON is defined by save_draft, so it is pinned within this chunk.

observations.what: In save_draft, the `paths` argument is documented as `list[str]` but the code calls `list(paths or [])` which would raise TypeError if paths is not iterable; however, the caller is expected to pass a list.
In save_draft, the `report` argument is documented as `dict` but the code calls `dict(report or {})` which would raise TypeError if report is not a mapping; again, expected to be a dict.
The slug generation in _slug strips leading/trailing hyphens but does not collapse consecutive hyphens, so an objective with many spaces could produce a slug with multiple hyphens; this is cosmetic.
list_drafts sorts by filename lexicographically; since timestamps are zero-padded and in UTC, this gives correct newest-first order.
set_status writes the entire draft dict back with indent=2, which may reformat the JSON even if nothing else changed; this is idempotent but could change formatting of existing drafts.
apply_payload calls set_status which may raise if the status is somehow not in _STATUSES, but since it passes 'applied' which is valid, it cannot raise.
